title: A smaller studio, a better workflow

cues.text: Interviewer: You went from twelve projects at once to four. What changed?
cues.rawText: Interviewer: You went from twelve projects at once to four. What changed?

cues.text: Maya: We were busy every day, but we kept finishing the week with nothing actually finished.
cues.rawText: Maya: We were busy every day, but we kept finishing the week with nothing actually finished.

cues.text: Maya: There were six different spreadsheets, three group chats, and a lot of people asking who had the latest version.
cues.rawText: Maya: There were six different spreadsheets, three group chats, and a lot of people asking who had the latest version.

cues.text: Maya: I thought we needed more people. What we really needed was fewer things open at the same time.
cues.rawText: Maya: I thought we needed more people. What we really needed was fewer things open at the same time.

cues.text: Interviewer: That sounds simple. Was it an easy decision to make?
cues.rawText: Interviewer: That sounds simple. Was it an easy decision to make?

cues.text: Maya: Not at all. Saying yes feels productive. Every new project looks like progress when it arrives in your inbox.
cues.rawText: Maya: Not at all. Saying yes feels productive. Every new project looks like progress when it arrives in your inbox.

cues.text: Maya: But the cost shows up later. You switch context, someone waits for feedback, and a small question holds up a whole day.
cues.rawText: Maya: But the cost shows up later. You switch context, someone waits for feedback, and a small question holds up a whole day.

cues.text: Maya: So we made one rule. A project only starts when we have the space to finish it.
cues.rawText: Maya: So we made one rule. A project only starts when we have the space to finish it.

cues.text: Interviewer: What did that look like on an ordinary Monday?
cues.rawText: Interviewer: What did that look like on an ordinary Monday?

cues.text: Maya: We put four cards on a wall. Each card had one owner, one next decision, and a definition of done.
cues.rawText: Maya: We put four cards on a wall. Each card had one owner, one next decision, and a definition of done.

cues.text: Maya: If a new request came in, we could point to the wall and ask which existing promise it should replace.
cues.rawText: Maya: If a new request came in, we could point to the wall and ask which existing promise it should replace.

cues.text: Maya: That question changed the conversation. We were finally choosing priorities instead of collecting them.
cues.rawText: Maya: That question changed the conversation. We were finally choosing priorities instead of collecting them.

cues.text: Interviewer: How did the team react to having fewer things on their plates?
cues.rawText: Interviewer: How did the team react to having fewer things on their plates?

cues.text: Maya: At first, people worried it would look like we were doing less. Then they started getting their afternoons back.
cues.rawText: Maya: At first, people worried it would look like we were doing less. Then they started getting their afternoons back.

cues.text: Maya: A designer could finish a draft before moving to another brief. Feedback arrived while the work was still fresh.
cues.rawText: Maya: A designer could finish a draft before moving to another brief. Feedback arrived while the work was still fresh.

cues.text: Maya: The best part wasn't a number on a dashboard. It was hearing someone say, I know what matters today.
cues.rawText: Maya: The best part wasn't a number on a dashboard. It was hearing someone say, I know what matters today.

cues.text: Interviewer: What would you tell another small studio trying this?
cues.rawText: Interviewer: What would you tell another small studio trying this?

cues.text: Maya: Start with the work you've already promised. Write down the next decision that would move each project forward.
cues.rawText: Maya: Start with the work you've already promised. Write down the next decision that would move each project forward.

cues.text: Maya: You don't need a perfect system. You need a shared view of what's happening and the courage to leave a little space.
cues.rawText: Maya: You don't need a perfect system. You need a shared view of what's happening and the courage to leave a little space.

cues.text: Maya: Busy is a feeling. Finished is something you can hand to another person.
cues.rawText: Maya: Busy is a feeling. Finished is something you can hand to another person.
